    Minimal projective presentations under finite orbit push-down #

    Finite skeletal orbit push-down preserves radical maps from indecomposable modules with trivial deck stabilizer. Applying this entrywise to a minimal finite-representable presentation proves that its pushed augmentation remains right minimal. The only presentation-specific input is trivial stabilizer for the representing summands.

    Orbit push-down preserves any minimal finite-representable projective cover under freeness on isomorphism classes. A fresh two-step presentation supplies the radical differential; uniqueness of projective covers transports the result to the specified cover.
